newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ECONOMIC GROWTH DOWN AS INTEREST RATES REMAIN UNCHANGED
Australia's annual rate of economic growth has fallen.
The national accounts for the September quarter show the annual rate now at 3.8 per cent.
Earlier today, the Reserve Bank adopted a cautious line on interest rates.
Following a board meeting yesterday, there was silence this morning from the bank at the usual time for any announcement on rates.
Long and short-term market interest rates rose a little in response.
But fixed interest director at CS First Boston, Tony Baildon, says it's still possible a move could come tomorrow.
He says the more common expectation is for a move in February, but no economist is willing to rule it out for this week, given the results coming out.
EUTHANASIA PATIENT'S SON STABLE AFTER HEART ATTACK
The son of the first person to die under the Northern Territory's euthansia laws, is in a stable condition in hospital after suffering a heart attack.
Rod Dent was taken to Bowral Hospital in the New South Wales southern Highlands at five O'clock this morning
Yesterday Mr Dent, a member of the Liberal Party, announced he'd no longer supported the right-to-die legislation, but denied he'd been subject to any political pressure.
Bowral Hospital manager, George Blackwall says Mr Dent's condition has been stabilised.
INTERPOL TO HELP TRACE BOY
Interpol has been called in to assist with the search for a 12-year-old youth, who was last seen at a Knoxfield school, in Melbourne's east almost three months ago.
Police say Benjamin Zaleski may have been kidnapped, and smuggled out of the country, after disappearing from the playground of the Carrington Primary School, in September.
Police say there's a possibility Ben is with someone he knows, and are investigating the contents of a letter received by his family, and believed to have been written by Ben.
Fears are held for the boy's psychological well-being, and police have again called for public assistance in helping to locate him.
HARRADINE'S TELSTRA IDEA REJECTED
Tasmanian Independent Senator, Brian Harradine, says he's not going to let his plans for Telstra rest, even though the Federal Government has officially rejected them.
Senator Harradine wants the Goverment to consider redeemable preference shares as a way of raising money from Telstra without selling it.
Treasurer, Peter Costello has formally notified Senator Harradine that the Government still wants to sell a third of Telstra.
With his vote crucial to the Government's plans, Senator Harradine says he still wants the Senate to consider his plan.
He's told ABC Radio the Treasurer's views are based on invalid assumptions.
NSW POLICE COMMISSIONER ASSUMING NEW POWERS
The New South Wales Police Commissioner is expected to assume new powers today to summarily sack officers that have lost his confidence.
The Governor will sign the controversial plans into law later today.
Commissioner Peter Ryan has identified a hit list of 96-unsuitable officers to be immediately removed, most having been named at the Wood Royal Commision.
The Police Minister's office says the purge won't begin until mid-December, after talks with the Police Association are complete.
COLSTON STAYING PUT AS INDEPENDENT FOR NOW
A representative of Independent Senator, Mal Colston, and his former Labor Party colleagues, are playing down suggestions he may return to the ALP fold.
Senator Colston's defection from Labor in August, strengthened the Government's legislative hand in the Upper House.
Queensland Labor Party Secretary, Mike Kaiser, says he understands an ALP conference on the Gold Coast last week invited Senator Colston to reapply to the party.
A spokeswoman for the Senator says he's not seeking to return to Labor at this stage, but he's never ruled out considering it in the longer term.
Labor leader Kim Beazley, says Senator Colston's recent record of voting against party policy would be taken into account if he did, but there's been no application from him.
And New South Wales Labor Senator Michael Forshaw says it's unlikely the party will support the former member playing the prodigal son, though he doesn't see any reason for that to occur.
RAILWAY OFFICIAL RECOGNISED JUDGE
A Sydney railway official says he was a bit horrified when he recognised a man accused of making sexual advances to two men, as a judge.
The railway official has told the Police Royal Commission he received both complaints about the late Judge David Yeldham at Wynyard Railway station, within a year
The official says in 1989 or 1990 a junior shop assistant accused a man of a sexual advance.
He said when spoken to the man identified himself as a judge, denied the complaint and agreed to wait for the police.
The second and similar complaint came from a 19-year old man.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
